i0-context.finding: Read epic 568 in full (7 work packages, 31 member issues, 5 exit criteria), the post-418 handoff (W1-W8), ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md, and queried all 31 member issues via gh: every one is OPEN.

q1-scope.title: How much of epic 568's 31 issues across 7 work packages is this run's scope?
q1-scope.imperative: The epic names 7 work packages and 31 member issues. Ask the human whether this run drives the whole epic to its exit criteria, or a named tranche (e.g. work packages 1+5 only) with the rest deferred. Recommend a tranche if the whole epic exceeds one run's session pool. Never self-answer.
q1-scope.finding: HUMAN: substrate plus the near-mechanical wins. In scope: WP1 lease lifecycle (552, 383, 357, 369, 318, 330, 208), WP2 binding store (441), WP5 postcondition cwd (315), plus the one-liners that need no substrate: 530 resolved worktree and 510 HARD-trip advisory text. Deferred: WP3 stop-rail attribution beyond 530, WP4 gauge/governor beyond 510, WP6 crew dispatch/liveness, WP7 pre-clearance and CLI hardening.

q2-prior-state.title: What has already landed against these 31 issues, and what does the tree actually look like now?
q2-prior-state.imperative: Resolve from the tracker and the code: which member issues are open, whether any partial fix already merged (e.g. PR #564 on spine_close), and which files carry the defects. Record code evidence.
q2-prior-state.finding: CODE EVIDENCE. All 31 member issues OPEN via gh; nothing partially landed. 552: my own scan of git ls-files spine.json finds 91 tracked spines carrying an engine_session, 24 still status=active (the issue title says 43 on disk -- different denominator, on-disk vs tracked; worth reconciling in the launch order). 441: scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py:83-103 _save_json_map -- its own docstring files the lock gap as KNOWN, NOT CHASED, and line 98 uses a shared tmp name path.name + .tmp, exactly the two gaps filed. 549: spine_rail.py:204-226 session_view merges the bare sid key with every sid#agent key via merged.update(entries), so a parent reads its descendants spines. 315: checklist_engine.py:775-799 _run_check_command calls subprocess.run with NO cwd= argument at all -- confirmed fail-open. 318: scripts/agent_work_root.py:110-141 durable_root returns the worktree fallback when _active_epic_lease(main_checkout) is true, which is the per-worktree siloing filed. Engine surface: checklist_engine.py 3352 lines, spine_rail.py 1052, mcp_spine_server.py 1269, run_crew.py 1663, spine_lifecycle.py 526, agent_work_root.py 150.

q3-self-modification.title: This epic edits the engine that every Commander in the epic is driving. How is that hazard handled?
q3-self-modification.imperative: checklist_engine.py, spine_rail.py, gauge_reader.py and the binding store are simultaneously the epic's subject and the fleet's running machinery. Ask the human how to handle self-modification: pin each worktree to an engine revision, serialize engine-core changes into a single non-concurrent wave, accept churn and re-verify at wave boundaries, or something else. Never self-answer.
q3-self-modification.finding: HUMAN: serialize engine-core, parallelize the rest. Changes touching scripts/checklist_engine.py, scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py and scripts/agent_work_root.py run one at a time in a narrow wave, with no concurrent Commander editing those three files. Everything else -- backfill scripts, the reaper, doctrine/advisory text, template edits -- fans out in parallel around them. Implication for wave cuts: engine-core issues (315, 357, 383, 549-adjacent, 441) are a serialized lane; 552 backfill, 208 harvest doctrine, 510 advisory text, 330/369 recovery doctrine are the parallel lane.

q4-ordering.title: What orders the waves — foundation first, cheapest first, or worst-bleeding first?
q4-ordering.imperative: Ask the human which ordering principle governs wave cuts, and whether the near-mechanical one-line fixes (#315 cwd threading, #530 resolved worktree) go early as a confidence wave or ride with their package. Never self-answer.
q4-ordering.finding: HUMAN: 315 first. Wave 1 is the cwd-threading fix in checklist_engine.py plus repair of every relative-check fallout across shipped spine templates, before any other engine-core work. Rationale accepted: fixing it late means every gate verified before it was verified under a check that could not fail. Wave 1 must therefore enumerate the blast radius by command and state the count -- every shipped template carrying a relative command check -- not by memory.

q5-checkpoints.title: Checkpoint protocol: stop-and-present at every wave boundary, or cleared through?
q5-checkpoints.imperative: Ask the human where the Admiral must stop and present, what reaches them at a checkpoint, and whether any wave is pre-cleared to run through. Never self-answer.
q5-checkpoints.finding: HUMAN: stop-and-present at every wave boundary. At each boundary I present what merged, what the evidence showed, and what the next wave proposes; the human clears the next launch. No wave is pre-cleared to run through.

q6-decision-classes.title: Which decision classes are delegated to the Admiral and which are surfaced?
q6-decision-classes.imperative: Walk the Decision Classes table: architecture/structural, scope change, merge to main, issue filing/closing, fix-now triage, spend/model tier, production defaults, apply-a-lesson. ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT says pushes/PRs/merges to main require explicit human approval unless pre-approved for the specified work — confirm whether this epic pre-approves them. Never self-answer.
q6-decision-classes.finding: HUMAN: merge to main is DELEGATED for this epic -- an explicit pre-approval under the ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md carve-out (pre-approved for the specified work). I merge PRs carrying a green check EXIT CODE plus an independent reviewer APPROVE, gate on the exit code and never chain a merge onto a watch command, and log every merge as a MERGE entry. Merges are still visible at each wave checkpoint. Remaining classes to be set in the contract per the recommendation and confirmed at sign-off.

q7-permissions.title: What harness permission pre-clearances does each delegated class need before wave 1?
q7-permissions.imperative: #408 and #145 are in this very epic: a delegated disposition does not bind the harness classifier. The post-418 run was refused `git branch -D`. Ask the human to pre-clear or record a fallback for each delegated class's external actions (gh pr merge, gh issue close, branch delete, push). Never self-answer.
q7-permissions.finding: HUMAN: pre-clear the merge path before wave 1. I draft allowlist entries for gh pr create / view / checks / merge, git push, and git branch -d and -D into .claude/settings.local.json and show them to the human before they are written. Grounding: the current allowlist holds only Bash(gh issue *) plus two python one-liners, so the delegated merge authority from q6 would otherwise be vetoed at the first ready PR -- 408 and 145 recurring on this epic own Admiral. Recorded fallback for anything still vetoed: one live approval in the moment, remaining equivalent actions batched to the next checkpoint, logged as ESCALATION.

q8-budget.title: Budget and model parameters: wave width, commander tier, crew tier, session-pool sizing.
q8-budget.imperative: Ask the human for commander/crew model tiers, how wide a wave may run, and whether to defer a wave past a usage-limit reset rather than launch into it. Never self-answer.
q8-budget.finding: HUMAN: narrow serialized core, 3-4 wide parallel. Engine-core lane runs ONE Commander at a time on Opus. Parallel lane runs up to 3-4 concurrent Commanders on Sonnet, escalating to Opus per issue where complexity, ambiguity or risk demands it, with the tier recorded in each launch order Budget slot. Usage-limit pool is a wave-sizing input: defer the next wave past a near reset rather than launching into it.

q9-success-shape.title: What does done look like, and is a measured negative an acceptable deliverable?
q9-success-shape.imperative: The epic states five exit criteria. Ask the human whether this run must demonstrate them by live repro, whether an honest null (a defect that does not reproduce, or a fix judged not worth its cost) closes an issue as a complete deliverable, and what the acceptance evidence is. Never self-answer.
q9-success-shape.finding: HUMAN: live repro before and after, honest null accepted. Each in-scope issue closes on a demonstrated repro that FAILS before the fix and PASSES after. A defect that does not reproduce, or a fix judged not worth its cost, is a COMPLETE successful deliverable when the measurement is stated -- not a failure. Scoped nulls apply: every verdict names what was tested and what was NOT tested. Targeted tests plus the relevant broader suite ride alongside per ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT, they do not replace the repro.

q10-expiry.title: When does the contract expire?
q10-expiry.imperative: Ask the human for a time or event expiry that forces a contract-refresh before further dispatch. Never self-answer.
q10-expiry.finding: HUMAN: contract expires after wave 1 merge. Wave 1 is the 315 cwd fix plus its template blast radius, the wave most likely to change what the rest of the tranche should look like, so the refresh happens as soon as it lands. No dispatch past that point without a confirmed contract refresh.

consolidation.summary: Latitude for epic 568 is settled with the human across 10 questions (8 decisions, 2 facts), all resolved, sign-off captured. Scope: substrate plus near-mechanical wins -- WP1 lease lifecycle, WP2 binding store, WP5 postcondition cwd, plus 530 and 510; WP3/4/6/7 deferred. Execution runs two lanes: engine-core files serialized one Commander at a time on Opus, everything else 3-4 wide on Sonnet. Wave 1 is 315 alone -- thread cwd into _run_check_command and repair the relative-check fallout across every shipped template, enumerated by command with a stated count. Stop-and-present at every wave boundary; merge to main delegated on green exit code plus independent APPROVE; merge-path permissions pre-cleared before wave 1 because the allowlist holds only gh issue *. Done means a repro that fails before and passes after, with an honest null accepted as a complete deliverable. Contract expires at wave 1 merge, so everything past wave 1 is forecast and gets a replan transition at that boundary. Contract written to .agent-work/epic-568/LATITUDE_CONTRACT.md.
